- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts show a gradual upward trend, but true outcomes often dip sharply after initial spikes or high values.
- Model fails to capture sharp downward corrections or sudden drops in price — especially after high historical values.
- Overshoots occur after spikes in history, where model continues rising while true price falls.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — overcorrects downward after high peaks, then fails to rebound.
- Forecasts lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in downward trends.
- Model overestimates the persistence of upward momentum, underestimating volatility and short-term reversals.
- True outcomes often show a “volatility cliff” — sharp drop after a peak, which model fails to anticipate.
- Model assumes linear or smooth progression, ignoring sudden regime shifts or policy-driven price drops.
- Forecasts are too optimistic in the early days of the 30-day window, then gradually adjust — but too late to catch sharp declines.
